title: Maximum Strength of a Group
statement:
`nums[i]` is the exam score of student `i`. Form one group by picking any non-empty set of students (a single student is allowed, and so is everyone). The group's strength is the product of the scores of its members.

Return the largest strength that any such group can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 13 scores you could try all `2^13` groups, but a few sign rules give the answer directly. Every positive score helps, so take all of them. Negative scores help only in pairs, and the best pairs use the largest magnitudes: after sorting, pair the most negative values from the left and drop a leftover odd negative (the one closest to zero). Zeros never help a product that is already positive. The only trouble is when nothing gets taken at all: then the group must still be non-empty, and the best single choice is the largest score (a `0` if there is one, or the lone negative).

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` ascending so negatives come first, most negative first.
2. Walk `i` in steps of two while `nums[i]` and `nums[i + 1]` are both negative, multiplying each pair into `product` and counting them in `taken`.
3. Multiply every positive `num` into `product` and count it.
4. If `taken` is still `0`, return the largest element, `nums[nums.length - 1]`.
5. Otherwise return `product`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted `nums` is `[-9, -5, -1, 2, 3, 5]`.

- `i = 0`: `-9` and `-5` are both negative, so `product = 45`, `taken = 2`.
- `i = 2`: `nums[3] = 2` is not negative, so the pairing stops; `-1` is left out.
- Positives `2`, `3`, `5` give `product = 45 · 30 = 1350`, `taken = 5`.

`taken > 0`, so the answer is `1350`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; both scans are O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- The group cannot be empty: `[-7]` gives `-7`, not `1`, and `[-5, 0]` gives `0`.
- With an odd number of negatives, drop the one nearest zero, not an arbitrary one; sorting and pairing from the left does this.
- The product can reach `9^13`, which needs a 64-bit integer in Java and C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product` | product of the scores chosen so far |
| `taken` | how many scores have been chosen |
| `i` | index of the first value of the current negative pair |
| `num` | the current value in the scan for positives |

narration.2: Sort ascending so the most negative values come first and can be paired.
narration.3: product holds the strength of the scores chosen so far.
narration.4: taken counts the chosen scores, so we know whether the group is empty.
narration.6: Take negatives two at a time while both members of the pair are negative.
narration.7: Two negatives multiply to a positive, so the pair always increases the strength.
narration.10: Now scan every value to pick up the positives.
narration.11: A positive score always makes the product larger.
narration.16: Nothing was chosen: only zeros and at most one negative exist.
narration.17: The best non-empty group is then the single largest score.
narration.19: Otherwise the chosen pairs and positives give the maximum strength.
